scope.boundary_rule: Twelve-hour scheduled collection window. Occurrence, publication/public-availability, collection and evidence-horizon times are distinct. Items occurring before the window are included only when materially new evidence became public inside the window. Later evidence updates existing events instead of duplicating occurrences.

new_events.summary: The IRGC said its air defenses shot down a U.S. MQ-9 over Qeshm Island at 02:29 local time using a new advanced air-defense system. Iranian reporting characterized it as the 52nd U.S. MQ-9 destroyed during the conflict. No immediate U.S. confirmation was identified in reviewed reporting. Preserve both the individual shootdown and cumulative 52-aircraft number as Iranian claims pending independent confirmation.

existing_event_updates.summary: Reuters reporting on September 16 said four vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from seven Monday. This extends the previously recorded single-digit/low-visible-traffic condition. Visible/AIS-derived counts remain lower-bound observations because dark or incomplete tracking can undercount actual movements.

Reuters reported Wang Yi urged Iran and the United States to return to the June/Islamabad memorandum, rebuild the negotiation mechanism on consensus already reached, conduct substantive consultations, and take effective measures to reopen Hormuz early. Code this as Chinese support for restoring the diplomatic framework and navigation, not as evidence China endorses literal reimplementation of every prior MoU concession or sequencing demanded by Tehran. Araghchi expressed openness to diplomacy while emphasizing Iranian rights and sovereignty.

Reuters, citing five sources, reported a weekend Muscat meeting involving U.S. officials and Houthi representatives, facilitated by Oman. Reporting identified senior Houthi figures including Mohammad Abdulsalam and Abdelmalik al-Ajiri. Sources said Houthis intended to uphold the 2025 U.S. ceasefire and avoid attacks on American vessels; reporting also described differentiated treatment of Saudi shipping. The State Department did not formally confirm the meeting. Preserve as multi-source wire reporting rather than official U.S. confirmation.

Reuters reported that Houthi gains consolidated strategic Red Sea coastline and islands around Bab el-Mandeb after Saudi-backed Yemeni units collapsed in sectors, with U.S.- and Saudi-supplied materiel reported abandoned or captured. Two Western officials were reported as saying the U.S. and European states were not prepared to provide direct military backing for a counteroffensive. Preserve territorial/materiel reporting separately from analytical labels about Saudi exposure or Iranian benefit.

Saudi Arabia maintained that the intercepted drone south of Mecca represented an attempted Houthi attack on the holy city and called protection of the holy sites a red line. Houthis denied targeting Mecca or religious sites. Pakistan and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation publicly condemned the alleged attack, but reviewed reporting did not establish Turkish or Pakistani military support to Saudi Arabia under the new defense pact. Intended aimpoint remains disputed despite regional diplomatic condemnation.

Reuters continued to report U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright's expectation that the East-West Pipeline could be flowing within days, while source estimates remained substantially longer for repairs and allowed for partial operation before full repair. Saudi restart time remained unconfirmed in reviewed material. Gulf equity reporting cited supply-reassurance reports involving crude shipment alternatives via Oman. Keep physical repair, partial flow, full throughput, Yanbu loading and alternative-route mitigation as separate states.

human_impact_updates.summary: Reporting citing OCHA said at least 18,000 families, around 125,000 people, had been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of September. The same reporting cited the U.N. human rights office for 40 civilian deaths in the escalation, including eight killed and 32 injured from September 1-14; women and children accounted for half of those killed and more than half of those injured. Preserve earlier >100,000, ~94,000 and 82,164 figures with their own horizons rather than overwriting them.

economic_energy_updates.observed_state: Reuters reported most Gulf equity markets lower on September 16 amid regional conflict risk, while Saudi equities were roughly flat and Aramco gained on supply-reassurance reporting. The market response is consistent with continuing energy-route risk but some expectation of mitigation. Do not treat market pricing as evidence of physical pipeline restoration.
